title: Paths of length up to the minimum degree
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with minimum degree $\delta(G)$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $k \le \delta(G)$. Then $G$ contains a path of length exactly $k$; that is, there exist vertices $u$ and $v$ and a path from $u$ to $v$ in $G$ traversing exactly $k$ edges.
hypotheses_covered: natural number k with k at most the minimum degree of G
